data.narrative:
Atopile is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Matthew Wildoer, Narayan Powderly, and Timothée Peter that has raised $500K to date. The relevant comp universe includes nine private robotics firms (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics) and one public comparable, though narrow peer alignment at the Seed stage limits direct benchmarking.

The valuation analysis relies primarily on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier to the $500K raised proxy, implying a $1.25M post-money value. This method is grounded in typical advancement multiples between Seed and subsequent rounds in early-stage capital markets. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient comparable data at identical or adjacent stages within the robotics sector—while ten same-sector peers exist, fewer than three qualified under strict stage and valuation-tier filters, preventing reliable median extraction.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $1.06M to $1.44M, with a median of $1.25M. This narrow range reflects methodological constraints rather than analytical confidence. Key uncertainties include the absence of closer-stage peers for comparative validation and limited disclosure of financial metrics (revenue, unit economics, or runway). The analysis would benefit from additional Seed-stage comparable transactions in adjacent robotics or manufacturing subsectors to narrow the range and stress-test the 2.5x multiplier assumption.
